newsitem.title: USA: Folgers says to raise 13 oz can of coffee.
newsitem.headline: Folgers says to raise 13 oz can of coffee.

text.p: Procter & Gamble's Folgers Coffee Co said it will raise the list price on its standard 13-ounce can by an additional 15 cents due to higher prices of green coffee on the world's futures markets.
The increase, which is to take effect immediately, brings the new price for a standard can to $2.86, the company said.
The latest retail price hike comes only one week after a 45-cent increase in the price of Folgers 13-ounce can of ground coffee took effect.

"The list price of Folgers coffee generally reflects the price of green coffee sold on the commodity market," Folgers said in a statement. "The market began increasing in January and reflects recent increases in green coffee costs."

The company said the commodity market's more than 50 percent surge since the start of the year was attributable to a number of factors including continued limited supplies of Central American coffees, a decrease in size estimates for the next Brazil coffee crop, dock strikes and threatened growers strikes in Colombia, and an announcement by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries of their intention to limit exports.

Folgers also announced it will raise its list price on its 13-ounce can of decaffeinated coffee 15 cents to $3.56, while instant coffee will go up 1.25 cents per ounce to $3.86 per eight-ounce can. Folgers Singles packets of coffee will increase by 10 cents per 19 count box, to $2.81.

"Even though Folgers does not set retail prices, for perspective, after this increase the average price of a cup of Folgers ground or instant prepared coffee prepared at home is still less than six cents a cup," the statement said.
